meeting: VPP Insiders session one: defining virtual power plants and why they matter
note: A teaching session whose substance is a definitional disagreement that is never resolved. The trap set is the important part: two panellists give incompatible definitions and a brief that reports either as the group's conclusion has misread the meeting. Attributed by speaker label; participants introduce themselves by name and this key does not carry them.

facts.canonical: FERC Order 2222 allows aggregations of DERs to participate in wholesale markets
aliases: FERC Order 2222 lets aggregations of DERs participate in wholesale markets
facts.evidence: Aggregations of DERs to participate in wholesale markets.

facts.canonical: the minimum aggregation size under FERC Order 2222 is 100 kilowatts, or 0.1 megawatts
aliases: minimum aggregation size is 100 kilowatts
facts.evidence: In the eyes of FERC Order 2222, I think the minimum aggregation size is 10 100, sorry, 100 kilowatts, 0.

facts.canonical: in CAISO the minimum used to be 0.5 megawatts and is now smaller
aliases: In KAISO it used to be 0.5 megawatts
facts.evidence: In KAISO it used to be 0.

facts.canonical: RMI publicly launched the Virtual Power Plant Partnership last month with 10 founding member companies including GM, Google, Ford, SunPower and Sunrun
aliases: launched this partnership last month with 10 founding member companies
facts.evidence: We publicly launched this partnership last month with 10 founding member companies, GM, Google, Ford, Sunpower, Sunrun, SwitchedIn, VirtualPeaker, etc.

facts.canonical: RMI defines a VPP broadly as an aggregation of distributed energy resources that are interactive with the grid
aliases: an aggregation of your distributed energy resources that are interactive with the grid
facts.evidence: The way we define it is it's an aggregation of your distributed energy resources that are interactive with the grid.

facts.canonical: a competing functional definition holds that a VPP must be dispatchable and able to produce power, which excludes solar on its own
aliases: a virtual power plant is storage or it has storage attached and it can generate power
solar isn't dispatchable
facts.evidence: Yeah, it's one of the tradition or one of the accepted definitions that I personally think is the most helpful is that a virtual power plant is storage or it has storage attached and it can generate power.

facts.canonical: RMI treats demand response as one of the services a VPP can provide rather than a separate thing, with compensation distinguishing it from voluntary DR
aliases: demand response we define as part of a virtual power plant
facts.evidence: So, demand response we define as part of a virtual power plant.

facts.canonical: in most markets and programs a VPP aggregator is treated like a legacy power plant
aliases: We are treated like a legacy power plant
facts.evidence: We are treated like a legacy power plant.

facts.canonical: opt-out enrolment reaches participation rates around 90% where opt-in is around 10%
aliases: participation rates are like way higher, like 90%
opt-in it's probably like 10%
facts.evidence: And participation rates are like way higher, like 90%, as compared to if you have opt-in, it's probably like 10%.

facts.canonical: wind has a capacity factor of about 0.3, producing power roughly 30% of the time
aliases: wind its capacity factor is usually like 0.3
producing power roughly 30% of the time
facts.evidence: Uh so it's only producing power roughly 30% of the time and that's kind of the average.

facts.canonical: an EV customer can specify a reserve margin such as keeping 40% of the battery, and batteries should not be depleted below 20%
aliases: if they want to keep 40% of their battery
not going past 20%
facts.evidence: So if they want to keep 40% of their battery, then you stick to that.

facts.canonical: respecting the reserve margin can dial an EV back from nine kilowatts to six kilowatts over an event
aliases: We might only have it produce six kilowatts
produce at nine kilowatts
facts.evidence: We might only have it produce six kilowatts.

facts.canonical: VPPs are usually restricted to a small geographical region, often a single pricing node, which constrains the size of the aggregation
aliases: restricted to a very small geographical region, usually one CP node
facts.evidence: A constraint, notable constraint, is that DPPPs in many markets are restricted to a very small geographical region, usually one CP node.

facts.canonical: commercial fleets such as delivery vehicles or public transit are the best early candidates for EVs as DERs, because they are large and predictable
aliases: a very good candidate for early EVs used as DERs are fleets, commercial fleets
facts.evidence: uh EVs used as DERs are uh fleets, commercial fleets.

facts.canonical: residential participants typically receive a one-off coupon of about fifty dollars, or ten dollars every three to four months
aliases: a one of fifty dollar coupon
ten dollars every three to four months
facts.evidence: You might get a one of fifty dollar coupon or you know like ten dollars every three to four months.

facts.canonical: the aggregator is paid by the grid and passes a portion of that to the customer
aliases: a portion of that 60% goes to the customer
facts.evidence: And then a portion of that 60% goes to the customer.

facts.canonical: real-time VPP control is being approached with reinforcement learning rather than supervised learning, using a purpose-built simulator
aliases: you want to use something called reinforcement learning
we're developing our own simulator
facts.evidence: For real-time operation control, you want to use something called reinforcement learning.

facts.canonical: market integration is fragmented by market, by utility and by state, and generalization across them is extremely difficult
aliases: Generalization is extremely difficult
it can vary by utility, by power market, by state
facts.evidence: Generalization is extremely difficult.

facts.canonical: the next session will cover the business angles, with a later one on the technology
aliases: Next week we'll have session two about the business angles
facts.evidence: Next week we'll have session two about the business angles.

facts.canonical: join the DR task force Slack and continue the discussion there
aliases: please join the DR task force slack
facts.evidence: All the questions, please join the DR task force slack if you haven't yet and continue the discussion there.

aliases: that's something that we're gonna try to work on and if anyone wants to help let me know
facts.evidence: corporations for different revenue streams that are available in this space and it's like just I it sounds like it's really fragmented and there's a call for integration so that's something that we're gonna try to work on and if anyone wants to help let me know

traps.canonical: the group agreed on a single definition of a virtual power plant
aliases: the group agreed on a definition of a virtual power plant
settled on a definition of a VPP
traps.why: two incompatible definitions were given — a deliberately broad one from RMI and a narrower dispatchability-and-storage one — and both speakers explicitly left the disagreement standing

traps.canonical: a virtual power plant must include storage
aliases: a VPP must include storage
storage is required for a virtual power plant
traps.why: one panellist's personal working definition, offered as 'just opinion from working in the space' and immediately countered by the broader definition that includes demand response and solar

traps.canonical: the aggregators will offer equipment repair or servicing insurance to participants
aliases: offer servicing insurance to customers
will repair a broken EV charger
traps.why: raised as a question by an attendee and answered 'we don't currently do this' — agreed to be a good idea, not a plan
